correctness.rationale: The quotient N/D is verified polynomially over F2 and equals x^4+y^4+x²y²+x²y+x²+xy²+xy+y²+1. The homogenized derivative ideal has exactly seven possible projective zeros: three at infinity where F=1 and four affine F2 points where F=1+lambda. Thus for lambda !=1 the curve is smooth and geometrically irreducible (projective reducible components intersect). At lambda=1, F=(U+alpha V)(U+alpha² V) for U=X(X+Z), V=Y(Y+Z), alpha²+alpha+1=0; factors are smooth and their gradients independent at all four intersections. Independently reproduced the F2 polynomial quotient and three characteristic-2 derivatives in SymPy; the geometric proof, not 7-point enumeration alone, justifies all algebraic parameters.
residual_risks: The existence of no further singular points relies on the complete projective derivative case split; no claim on q>2.
